stem:
Neel studies this cryptarithm. Each letter stands for a digit, and different letters stand for different digits.

$$\begin{array}{c@{}c} & A & B \\ + & A & B \\ \hline & C & A \end{array}$$

Which claim correctly narrows a digit before trying every full substitution?

options.text: Letter $C$ must be twice letter $A$, with no carry anywhere.
Any digits for $A$, $B$, and $C$ work as long as each letter is a single digit.
From the units column, $A$ equals the units digit of $2B$ after the carry is placed, so each choice of $B$ leaves only one possible $A$.
The sum $CA$ must be smaller than one addend $AB$.

teacher.key_rationale: Doubling $AB$ forces the units digit of $2B$ (with carry) to be $A$, so $B$ narrows $A$ before a full search. $C$ is not simply $2A$ with no carry, not every digit triple works, and $CA=2\cdot AB$ is larger than $AB$.
